answer: To block fake clones, a marketplace can require every account to post a rolling custody bond and sign a hash proof over a unique data slice each 1 round. Consider a mesa exchange where bots ship vine oil down to a sheltered inlet under a strict quorum threshold. Every active bot must lock 60 tokens and pass a custody audit every 6 hours, or its bond is 100% slashed. An honest operator with 1 bot locks 60 tokens once and gets 100% back, whereas an attacker with 500 fake bots must lock 30,000 tokens linear to fleet size. One limitation is that bond locks slow new signups.
